resources.string: Choose a destination, connection, device and input to enable Connect and play.

Select a paired PC above or choose Pair a new PC.

No USB gamepad detected. Connect one through USB-C.

Move with one finger and tap for a left click. Use two fingers to right-click, scroll or pinch to zoom. Swipe three fingers up for Task View or to restore minimized windows, down to return from Task View or minimize all windows, or sideways to choose a window.
← Use Android Back to open the session menu
Choose your destination and connect over Bluetooth or Wi-Fi. Virtual and physical controls work together automatically.
• For a new PC, allow phone visibility and add the phone in its Bluetooth settings.
• Use the virtual gamepad or connect a physical controller to the phone.
Bluetooth HID support varies by Android device and may require Steam configuration. Wi-Fi requires BridgePad Desktop. USB output is not available yet.

Reads compatible USB HID controllers directly. You can leave the app or turn off the screen. This is input from the controller, not USB output to the PC.

Connect a data cable and enable USB tethering in Android settings. BridgePad will use the Desktop protocol over the cable; Wi-Fi is not required.
Choose the controls you want to use on this phone.
Customize the position and size of the controls shown while playing.
Use the area around the camera
Uses the complete display, including the camera cutout and Android navigation gesture edges.
The larger area may slightly reposition some controls. The camera itself remains unavailable. You can adjust the result in the layout editor.
Tap a control to select it. Drag the side handles to change one dimension or a corner handle to change both.
Choose a ready-made layout, then customize it if you want. Changes are only applied when saved.
All changes made since opening the editor will be lost.

Drag vertically to move layout options

Test the upcoming BridgePad Desktop connection over your local network.

Start the diagnostic BridgePad Desktop receiver on a PC connected to the same network. Enter its local IP address, port and certificate fingerprint below. The test sends 250 encrypted Ping/Pong samples at 125 Hz.
Copy the complete fingerprint printed by BridgePad Desktop. A different certificate will be rejected.
%1$s · handshake %2$s ms\nRTT p50 %3$s ms · p95 %4$s ms · p99 %5$s ms\n%6$d samples
Run the existing encrypted Desktop protocol through Android USB tethering and verify the actual socket route.

Connect the data cable, enable USB tethering in Android settings, and turn off Wi-Fi on the phone for an unambiguous test. Run the Desktop daemon, enter the PC address assigned on the USB adapter and its certificate fingerprint. This uses the same encrypted protocol and playable session as Wi-Fi.

Compare RFCOMM and BLE GATT before selecting the production Bluetooth Desktop transport.

Run the matching BridgePad Bluetooth spike on the paired PC first. Each test streams 1,000 reports at 125 Hz. Desktop measures delivery and cadence; lightweight periodic pings measure RTT and keep the duplex link active. Direct HID remains off during this diagnostic.
End the current gameplay session before testing. HID and Desktop output must never be active together.

Test the Android Open Accessory candidate before selecting the production USB transport.

Install this build before starting the Desktop spike. Connect an unlocked phone with a data cable, run bridgepad-usb-spike on the PC, approve the Android USB permission and then run this 250-sample test at 125 Hz. ADB may disconnect while accessory mode is active.
